Music player design-only review · native Slint study · 2026-09-23

Three separate command-bar questions

D21 settles that a command bar exists. Its optional global hotkey is configurable and off by default; an in-app binding remains available when global registration is off. D25 reserves Ctrl+F for future search and Ctrl+O for the folder picker, but does not decide whether search shares the command surface. Exact shortcut assignment and any visible in-app entry still need their own design pass.

Reply with one I code, one G code, and one R code, plus corrections. In-app placement and global invocation can coexist; R decides only whether Ctrl+F uses a separate search destination or an explicit search mode in the same command surface.

The captures are native, nonfunctional Slint at the desktop app’s current preferred 480 × 600px size, in light and dark. A2 keeps this project on baseline MD3: the expanded docked Search view has a 28px outer shape, flat 56px header and divider; the full-content version has sharp outer corners and a 72px header. The 56px full pill belongs to the collapsed Search bar, not another pill nested inside the expanded view. Baseline list rows are square; the outlined keyboard-current row is a custom desktop focus cue, not a persistent selection. Roboto and official Material icons render the native study.

The 1100 × 640px samples are stress viewports, not a default-window-size choice. At 360px, the docked choice reflows to the full-content treatment rather than squeezing below the minimum. Global scenes draw a second-window concept inside one Slint scene, not an actual OS overlay or hotkey implementation. Static rasters do not validate keyboard interaction, screen-reader semantics, window focus restoration, search indexing, or action execution. Compact desktop docking and keeping the player header in the full-content variant are stated adaptations from Android’s default full-screen focused search.

I · In-app command surface, player already focused

In-app ranking: I1 > I2 > I3. I1 retains a clearer source anchor than I2; I2 keeps more of the player visually present than I3.

G · When the optional global hotkey is enabled and another app was active

Global ranking: G2 > G1. G2 protects the ongoing task; G1 is more contextual but takes over the screen.

R · Relationship to the future Ctrl+F search surface

Search relationship ranking: R1 > R2. R1 gives navigation a dedicated space; R2 reuses the palette but asks people to track modes. D25 itself does not settle either choice.

In-app comparison at the preferred desktop size

All I variants show the same typed action query, open, and the same selected result. The thumbnail follows your system scheme; preview either native capture at 100%.

Out-of-app invocation concepts

Both G variants start from the same previous app and the same typed action query. Their window and focus behavior is proposed, not tested by these screenshots.

Search invoked by Ctrl+F

Both R variants show the same illustrative query and result types. Folder results open a folder; track results reveal a track. Whether folder paths match queries, which media types are indexed, and result ranking are separate open questions; the D31 picker remains the browsing route.

Fit and state probes, not additional choices

I variants also appear at 1100 × 640px; I1 reflows to a full-content baseline Search view at 360 × 640px with larger text and a long action. Separate I1 captures show no results and an explicitly unavailable action. All are native Slint in both schemes.
